title: CITE-seq
scope: Original Stoeckius 2017 CITE-seq implementation represented by the CITE-Seq row: DNA-tagged surface antibodies combined with Drop-seq capture of cellular mRNA. The row ends at size-separated mRNA-derived cDNA and antibody-derived DNA-tag fractions. Its terminal caption describes their linked readout; downstream adapter completion, sequencing and computational processing are not additional drawn operations. DroNc-seq above, ECCITE-seq below and the unrelated right-hand chemical/QR legend are contextual material, not target alternatives.

method_scopes.rationale: The assigned card and central row identify CITE-seq. The original paper names the method and identifies its Figure 1b route as CITE-seq combined with Drop-seq, matching the depicted cells, oligobeads, lysis/capture and size-separated DNA products. All five local operations belong to this scoped depiction. Drop-seq is the embedded capture implementation, not another target method. The prepared antibody-complex and bead insets define incoming materials, without depicting their manufacture. The paper also describes 10x implementations; those do not expand this row or imply that all CITE-seq implementations have this exact preparation history. The antibody reporters are DNA templates, and their copied products remain distinguished from mRNA-derived cDNA.
